subject: Marketplace listing: final evidence & support SLA matrix for Finlytics
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rachel from AWS Partner Network <rachel@aws-partners.com>, Azure Marketplace Ops <azuremarketplaceops@microsoft.com>, GCP Partner Success <gcp-partner-success@google.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing: final evidence & support SLA matrix for Finlytics

Hi all,

We're finalizing the marketplace listing and co-sell materials for Finlytics (Finlytics Inc.). Before we push the listing drafts, can you confirm the exact evidence packages each cloud needs for: branding/claims approval, support SLA statements, and any required runbooks for incident escalation?

I've attached a working support SLA matrix (marketplace_support_matrix.xlsx) and the current listing draft for AWS (aws_listing_draft.docx). High-level asks: 
- AWS: do you need separate GRC attestation or is our SOC2 cert + the listing artifacts sufficient?
- Azure: what language is required for support hours and critical response times (P1/P2)?
- GCP: any specific branding placement rules beyond the logo/alt-text spec?

Timeline: Finlytics expects the marketplace to go live the week of July 5. We need final vendor approvals by June 25 to hit that.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Cloud Partnerships (Go-to-Market)
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel from AWS Partner Network <rachel@aws-partners.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: final evidence & support SLA matrix for Finlytics

Jordan —

Quick answers inline: 
- Branding/claims: we require the logo files, a short 25-word description and any marketing claims to be substantiated. For claims like "enterprise-grade inference" we ask for a performance benchmark doc or customer testimonial (anonymized is fine).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II plus a short operational runbook is usually sufficient for the listing. For co-sell, bring the AWS Partner Manager on the call with the customer; additional GRC docs may be requested during procurement but not strictly for the listing.
- Support SLA language: you can use a regionalized statement (e.g., "24x7 support for P1, next-business-day for P3") but call out escalation path and expected response windows in hours. We'll flag ambiguous phrasing during review.

I've attached the AWS checklist in comments (see aws_listing_draft.docx). I can also run a quick redline if you push the final draft by Thursday.

Regards,
Rachel
AWS Partner Network
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing: final evidence & support SLA matrix for Finlytics

Team —

I pulled together answers for Azure and GCP in the attached matrix and a short draft policy response (azure_policy_response.pdf). Highlights:
- Azure needs explicit RTO/RPO language for support tiers if we claim a "24x7 L1/L2 escalation"; they prefer numeric response-time commitments (e.g., 1hr P1, 4hr P2).
- Branding: Azure enforces a placement hierarchy (product logo above fold, no co-mingled vendor badges). Our current modal screenshot will need repositioning.
- GCP: they flagged an earlier listing for the phrase "real-time inference"; recommend we change to "sub-second median latency for common prompts" and include the benchmark doc.

Next steps I propose: Vanessa to update the support SLA matrix with numeric windows, Jordan to share a sanitized benchmark PDF and marketing claim substantiation, Marissa to prepare the final listing copy for AWS/Azure/GCP with alternate wording for the flagged claims.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Adding the draft copy for AWS with the edited claim language below. I'm dropping the phrase "real-time inference" as suggested and using a measured phrasing. Also attached branding_assets_v2.zip with final screenshots and logo variations.

--- draft excerpt (for AWS listing) ---
Redwood Inference powers Finlytics' on-demand analytics pipeline, delivering sub-second median token latency for typical query sizes. Backed by SOC2 Type II controls and enterprise support with defined escalation paths.
--- end excerpt ---

Marissa will coordinate a short call with the Finlytics procurement team to confirm support hours and their expectations. Suggested call times: Fri 18 Jun 11:00-12:00 PT or Mon 21 Jun 09:00-10:00 PT.

Marissa Cole

If you send updated matrix + the benchmark PDF in the next hour, my team will pre-read before the call.

— Priya N., Finlytics Procurement
